account: Transport for West Midlands enabled VivaCity near-miss detection in 40 sensors and used the observations to select and implement road-layout changes. The source reports 61,000 detected near misses in six months and the installation of measures including central islands and narrower junction mouths. The interventions are documented, but the source does not establish a reduction in collisions or injuries. On 5 February 2025 Coventry City Council was still set to install a pedestrian refuge at Grange Road after the sensors recorded near misses there. On 18 November 2025 TfWM reported that near misses at the junction fell from 17 to 2 over equal two-month periods after the refuge was built, a cut of more than 88 percent. TfWM gave no data on collisions or injuries.

ai_role.statement: The sensors detected near misses and supplied the data that TfWM used to choose the Grange Road site and work out how to reduce them. Coventry City Council built the refuge with TfWM funding, and TfWM credits the refuge with slowing turning traffic. The same sensors measured the result, so the 88 percent figure depends on the detector that chose the site.
